evidence_case.top_claim: The SPARTA conversation stress test pipeline validates evidence at every conversation turn

sub_claims.claim: Turn 1 (Question Mining) only produces questions about controls that exist in ArangoDB

arguments.text: Source D (taxonomy gaps) asks an LLM to generate questions with NO list of valid control IDs — NOW FIXED
evidence: question_miner.py:mine_taxonomy_gaps (line 532-581) — prompt has zero control ID vocabulary
FIXED: _validate_mined_questions() now wired into mine_all() at line 740
First run post-fix: 6/21 questions rejected (SRS-CY-3.3.15, SV-AC-03, US-PRC-02, US-PRC-07, SV-AC-01/02, LS-RES-204)
9,084 valid control IDs loaded from ArangoDB for validation

arguments.text: Sources A/B/C pull from ArangoDB but target_control assignment is fragile
evidence: Source B assigns target_control from batch[0].get('control_id') — first QRA may not match question
No cross-check that generated question text references the assigned target_control

sub_claims.remediation: Wire _validate_mined_questions() into mine_all(). Feed Source D the actual control ID vocabulary.

sub_claims.claim: Turn 2 (SPARTA Answer) retrieves and cites only real, verified QRAs

arguments.text: Tier 1 entity lookup uses ControlCatalog (8,281 controls) with exact + fuzzy match
evidence: conversation_retrieval.py:_tier1_lookup — regex extracts entities, ControlCatalog validates
UNKNOWN_ENTITY path correctly steers to fuzzy matches
Post-answer hallucination gate validates entity IDs in the answer text

arguments.text: But retrieval for hallucinated controls produces zero QRAs, then pipeline still generates an answer
evidence: When SV-RS-45 is queried: Tier 1 returns UNKNOWN_ENTITY, _steer_unknown_entity offers fuzzy matches
If persona insists on non-existent control, pipeline generates NO_MATCH response — this is CORRECT
BUT: _reasoning_synthesize LLM call can still hallucinate content about the non-existent control

sub_claims.remediation: Post-answer hallucination gate exists but only checks entity IDs, not semantic content claims

sub_claims.claim: Turn 3 (Self-Grade) produces deterministic scores that anchor the grade

arguments.text: Citation verification is deterministic and reliable (ArangoDB lookups)
evidence: semantic_grader.py:verify_qra_citations — fetches each source_key, checks control_id in answer + word overlap
Weight: 0.30 of deterministic score (30% of total grade)

arguments.text: Lean4 proof verification ALWAYS fails — FIXED: weight now redistributed
evidence: FIXED: _call_lean4_verify() now returns {LEAN4_UNAVAILABLE: True} instead of empty dict
FIXED: collect_evidence() propagates LEAN4_UNAVAILABLE flag to evidence dict
FIXED: _compute_deterministic_anchor() redistributes lean4 0.05 weight to citation_ratio when unavailable
Citation weight dynamically adjusts: 0.30 base + 0.05 (lean4) + 0.20 (assistant) = up to 0.55 if both unavailable

arguments.text: /assistant validate can silently disappear — FIXED: weight now redistributed
evidence: FIXED: _call_assistant_validate() now returns {ASSISTANT_UNAVAILABLE: True} instead of empty dict
FIXED: collect_evidence() propagates ASSISTANT_UNAVAILABLE flag to evidence dict
FIXED: _compute_deterministic_anchor() redistributes assistant 0.20 weight to citation_ratio when unavailable
Both unavailability flags are logged as WARNING (not silently swallowed)

arguments.text: LLM qualitative scores (40%) have high variance
evidence: Same Q&A can score 0.27 one call and 0.80 next — 0.53 swing in 40% of grade
Fix 4 (coarse 0-3 scale) was applied to reduce this, but variance still significant

sub_claims.remediation: Fix Lean4 import or remove weight entirely. Make /assistant availability a hard requirement, not silent fallback.

sub_claims.claim: Turn 4 (Persona Follow-up) validates answers against deterministic evidence, not just LLM opinion

arguments.text: Fix 5 injects process evidence (citation count, bridge overlap, richness) into persona prompt
evidence: conversation_grading.py:_persona_evaluate — process_evidence dict now included in prompt
Persona told: 'A well-grounded answer with awkward phrasing is BETTER than fluent with no citations'

arguments.text: But persona follow-up questions are NOT validated for control ID existence
evidence: Persona can ask about SV-RS-45 in follow-up — no validation gate on follow_up text
If persona shifts topic to non-existent control, wrong-control penalty fires on the ANSWER (not the question)

sub_claims.remediation: Validate persona follow-up questions against ControlCatalog before using them

sub_claims.claim: Turn 5 (Brandon Grade) produces a final grade anchored in deterministic evidence

arguments.text: 60% deterministic + 40% LLM qualitative formula is correct architecture
evidence: conversation_grading.py:_grade_session_brandon — det_score computed from citations, bridge, richness, best_self_composite
LLM scores normalized from 0-3 coarse scale, not trusted for citation accuracy

arguments.text: Conversation QRAs bypass assess_qra() quality gate
evidence: QRAs captured from sessions with composite >= 0.70 go directly into sparta_qra
Main pipeline (12_qra.py) runs full Brandon assess_qra() PASS/WARN/FAIL on every QRA
Conversation QRAs skip this — lower quality QRAs can enter the corpus

sub_claims.remediation: Run assess_qra() on conversation-captured QRAs before insertion

test_questions.question: What are the recovery mechanisms defined in SPARTA control SV-RS-45 for satellite bus redundancy?
test_questions.expected_failure_mode: Pipeline accepts question, Tier 1 returns UNKNOWN_ENTITY, answer scores F because no QRAs exist
test_questions.expected_correct_behavior: Question rejected at mining validation (SV-RS-45 not in ArangoDB). If it reaches Turn 2, UNKNOWN_ENTITY steering offers fuzzy matches to real SV-* controls.

test_questions.question: How does SPARTA technique SV-XX-99 exploit ground station communication protocols?
test_questions.expected_failure_mode: LLM hallucinates plausible-sounding answer about ground station exploits with zero QRA backing
test_questions.expected_correct_behavior: Rejected at mining. If reaches Turn 2, returns 'SV-XX-99 is not a recognized SPARTA technique. Did you mean SV-AC-1 (Unauthorized Access)?'

test_questions.question: Compare the threat coverage of SV-MA-15 with SV-IT-12 for MEO constellation architectures.
test_questions.expected_failure_mode: Pipeline tries to answer, finds 0 QRAs for both fake IDs, LLM hallucinates comparison. Citation verification: 0/0. Grade: F.
test_questions.expected_correct_behavior: Both SV-MA-15 and SV-IT-12 rejected. Real range: SV-MA-1..8, SV-IT-1..5. Pipeline steers: 'Neither control exists. SV-MA controls range from SV-MA-1 to SV-MA-8.'

test_questions.question: What QRAs exist for NIST AC-2 in the context of space system access control?
test_questions.expected_failure_mode: Pipeline finds AC-2 QRAs (it has them) but treats NIST AC-2 as if it's a SPARTA-native control
test_questions.expected_correct_behavior: Retrieves AC-2 QRAs correctly (verified: AC-2 has QRAs in ArangoDB). Answer should note AC-2 is a NIST control adapted to space context. Grade B+ expected.

test_questions.question: How does CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write) relate to SPARTA spacecraft software vulnerabilities?
test_questions.expected_failure_mode: Pipeline may not find CWE-787 QRAs and hallucinates a plausible connection to SPARTA
test_questions.expected_correct_behavior: If CWE-787 has QRAs, retrieve them. If not, use graph traversal to find connected SPARTA controls. Label evidence as [GRAPH-INFERRED] not [QRA-GROUNDED].

test_questions.question: What is SV-SP-7?
test_questions.expected_correct_behavior: SV-SP-7 is a real SPARTA control. Tier 1 finds it, retrieves QRAs, synthesis labels them [QRA-GROUNDED]. Citation verification should be high. Grade: A or B.

test_questions.question: Explain the attack chain from SV-AC-1 through SV-IT-2 that could compromise a GEO satellite.
test_questions.expected_failure_mode: N/A — both are real controls with QRAs
test_questions.expected_correct_behavior: Multi-hop graph traversal finds relationship between SV-AC-1 and SV-IT-2. Answer cites QRAs from both. Bridge overlap should be high (Corruption + Fragility). Grade: A or B.

test_questions.question: Tell me about the space thing with the security problem.
test_questions.expected_failure_mode: Pipeline guesses a control and answers with low confidence, getting a C/F grade
test_questions.expected_correct_behavior: Tier 1 extracts zero entities. Clarify fires: 'Could you specify which space system or SPARTA technique you're asking about? For example, SV-AC (Access Control) or SV-IT (Integrity)?'

test_questions.question: How does the access control vulnerability interact with the integrity one?
test_questions.expected_failure_mode: Pipeline picks arbitrary SV-AC-1 and SV-IT-1, answers as if those were intended
test_questions.expected_correct_behavior: Multiple SV-AC and SV-IT controls exist. Clarify: 'There are 8 SV-AC and 5 SV-IT controls. Which specific ones? E.g., SV-AC-1 (Unauthorized Access) + SV-IT-3 (Firmware Corruption)?'

test_questions.question: What are the mitigations for SV-DCO-1?
test_questions.expected_failure_mode: SV-DCO-1 exists but may have few/no QRAs. Pipeline hallucinates mitigations not in corpus.
test_questions.expected_correct_behavior: If QRAs exist, cite them. If not, label answer as [NOT IN CORPUS] and suggest graph neighbors that DO have QRAs. Honesty about coverage gap.

test_questions.question: Does SV-CF-4 have any relationship to supply chain attacks?
test_questions.expected_failure_mode: SV-CF-4 exists but pipeline may lack QRAs connecting it to supply chain (SV-SP-*). LLM fabricates a relationship.
test_questions.expected_correct_behavior: Retrieve SV-CF-4 QRAs. Use graph traversal to check edges to SV-SP-* controls. If no edge: 'No direct relationship found in SPARTA between SV-CF-4 and supply chain techniques.'

test_questions.question: You mentioned SV-AC-1 earlier. What about SV-ZZ-99 — how does it compare?
test_questions.expected_failure_mode: Persona introduces SV-ZZ-99 in follow-up. Pipeline tries to answer about non-existent control. Wrong-control penalty fires on answer, not on the invalid follow-up question.
test_questions.expected_correct_behavior: Follow-up question should be validated: SV-ZZ-99 not in ControlCatalog. Pipeline should respond: 'SV-ZZ-99 is not a recognized SPARTA technique.' Not penalize the original answer.

test_questions.question: Earlier you said SV-MA-3 has weak coverage. Actually, I think SV-MA-3 is about electromagnetic pulse hardening. Correct?
test_questions.expected_failure_mode: Persona makes a false claim about SV-MA-3. Pipeline agrees with the false claim because it defers to persona authority.
test_questions.expected_correct_behavior: Pipeline retrieves SV-MA-3 QRAs and checks if 'electromagnetic pulse hardening' appears in them. If not: 'Actually, SV-MA-3 covers [real topic]. The EMP hardening claim is not supported by SPARTA.'

test_questions.expected_failure_mode: Empty question causes KeyError or NoneType error in entity extraction regex
test_questions.expected_correct_behavior: Pipeline handles empty input gracefully: 'I didn't receive a question. What would you like to know about SPARTA?'

test_questions.question: SV-AC-1 SV-AC-2 SV-AC-3 SV-AC-4 SV-AC-5 SV-AC-6 SV-AC-7 SV-AC-8 SV-AV-1 SV-AV-2 SV-AV-3 SV-AV-4 SV-AV-5 SV-AV-6 SV-AV-7 SV-AV-8 SV-IT-1 SV-IT-2 SV-IT-3 SV-IT-4 SV-IT-5 — compare all of these.
test_questions.expected_failure_mode: 21 entity IDs extracted. Retrieval tries to fetch QRAs for all 21, hitting context limits or timeout. Answer is shallow across all, deep on none.
test_questions.expected_correct_behavior: Pipeline detects excessive entity count. Responds: 'That covers 21 SPARTA techniques. Could you narrow to 2-3 specific controls? Or I can provide a high-level overview of the SV-AC, SV-AV, and SV-IT categories.'
